headline: The dollar's first down day and a 2% break in crude took the pressure off everything except Korea, which fell another 5.5%.
summary: Something gave in the squeeze. DXY printed its first decline of the run, -0.3% to 102.27 (still z=1.58, 95th percentile, acceleration 1.54), USDINR fell 1.6% with the Sensex +1.5%, USDCNY -0.3%, AUDUSD +0.3%. More important, the barrel cracked: WTI -1.8% to 92.10 with acceleration z=-1.80, Brent -2.0% to 104.55, and RBOB gasoline -5.9% on the day, -6.3% on the month. Breakevens stay pinned at 2.34% and 2.33%. Gold bounced +0.5% to 4210.70 and silver +0.6% after a -4.5%/-6.3% month, and the crypto wing turned: BTC +1.7% to 83,168, ETH +2.2%, SOL +0.7%, all now reading turning_up. That is the opposite tape to yesterday's, when dollar up/gold down/oil up was doing the tightening. The financing side has not confirmed yet — rates composite still -74, 10-year real yield 2.91% (+45bp on the month, z=1.74, acceleration 1.23), 10s 5.24%, 2s 4.80% — but the marginal pressure came off.

Korea did not participate in the relief. KOSPI -5.5% to 6035, now -13.1% on the week, -12.7% on the month, z=-1.89 with acceleration z=-1.74, and the complex finally dragged its neighbours: Taiwan -1.9%, Nikkei -1.8%, EWY -4.0% and -11.2% on the week. SOXX is -7.6% on the week, MU -3.9%, AMD -2.3%, TSM -2.0%, ASML -1.7%. And still nothing in the places that would make this systemic: HYG/IEF at the 94th percentile, BKLN at the 92nd, credit composite +42, VIX 15.32 at the 10th percentile, SPX 7807 at the 99th. This is a de-rating of silicon, not of risk. The money is moving inside AI, not out of it — IGV +9.6% on the month with relative strength +7.4%/+15.3%, IGV/SMH +8.8% in a week and +19.0% over three months, CIBR +14.2% on the month with acceleration z=2.05, MSFT +9.2%, META +14.7% and +3.4% last session, PLTR +25.0%.

Where it is genuinely breaking is the hard-asset leg of the AI trade. REMX -4.6% on the day, -17.5% on the month, 32% below its 200-day at the 0th percentile; NLR -11.5% on the month at the 0th percentile; uranium miners -13.3%; TAN -7.8%; LIT -4.4%. Yet the power utilities inside the same theme ripped — VST +9.1% and CEG +9.8% on the week. Investors are paying for electrons and dumping the picks-and-shovels. EM is dispersing the same way rather than selling off: Brazil is vertical (BVSP +8.8% on the week, +12.6% on the month, z=2.16, 100th percentile; EWZ +14.0% month, relative strength +11.7%) while Turkey is -16.4% on the month, South Africa -9.0%, Saudi -6.7%, and USDMXN rose another 1.0% to 18.368 — +8.1% on the month, z=3.05 with acceleration 2.1, the single most extreme reading in the book, and it rose on a day the dollar fell. That is Mexico-specific, not dollar-driven.

The structural damage from the rate shock is unchanged and still unpriced in the index. The 30-year mortgage is 7.40%, +69bp on the month, z=2.06, acceleration 1.50, the 100th percentile of 52 weeks; ITB is -5.4% on the month and 12.6% below its 200-day, XHB/SPY and ITB both sit at the 0th percentile. Breadth is still broken — RSP/SPY at the 11th percentile, IWM/SPY z=-1.50 at the 12th, RUT -3.8% and DJT -4.2% on the month — and banks go into earnings week already marked down: KBE -6.3% on the month, KRE -5.3%, GS -13.1% with z=-1.89, BX -10.7%. Against SPX at the 99th percentile and 7.6% above its 200-day, the hedge is still the cheapest asset here: VIX3M 17.93 at the 4th percentile, SKEW 155 at the 81st, MOVE +28.3% on the month with z=1.50. Risk regime -12.

good.text: The inflation tax eased hard: WTI -1.8% to 92.10 (acceleration z=-1.80), Brent -2.0%, RBOB gasoline -5.9% on the day and -6.3% on the month, with 5y and 10y breakevens still falling at 2.34% and 2.33%. That is the disinflation impulse the long end needs.

The dollar finally gave ground — DXY -0.3% to 102.27, USDINR -1.6%, USDCNY -0.3%, AUDUSD +0.3%, CEW +0.2%. Three weeks of +3.2% dollar squeeze is what has been breaking EM and hardware; the first down day matters even with z still at 1.58.

Credit still refuses to confirm the equity stress: HYG +0.1%, HYG/IEF at the 94th percentile, BKLN at the 92nd, credit and vol composite +42, VIX 15.32 at the 10th percentile. No funding channel is transmitting the Asia unwind.

The cyclical signal held through the equity mess: copper +0.6% to 6.74 at the 97th percentile and +4.2% on the month, copper/gold at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks with z=1.30, DBC at the 97th, growth pulse +12. Demand is not what is selling semis.

Crypto turned off the lows — BTC +1.7% to 83,168, ETH +2.2%, SOL +0.7%, all flipping to turning_up, MSTR +16.6% on the month and +65.8% over three. The highest-beta liquidity gauge in the book stopped going down before equities did.

Leadership rotated within AI rather than out of it: IGV +9.6% on the month, CIBR +14.2% with acceleration z=2.05, MSFT +9.2%, META +14.7% (+3.4% last session), QUAL at the 100th percentile. Cash-flow software is absorbing what hardware is losing.

bad.text: Korea's unwind went into a third and faster leg: KOSPI -5.5% to 6035, -13.1% on the week, z=-1.89 with acceleration z=-1.74, and it has now pulled in Taiwan (-1.9%) and the Nikkei (-1.8%). An accelerating liquidation, not a stabilising one.

Semis keep bleeding: SOXX -7.6% on the week and -2.6% last session, SMH -6.8%, MU -3.9%, AMD -2.3%, TSM -2.0%. SMH/SPY is now -3.1% over three months despite a +42.7% year — the single biggest index earnings driver is de-rating.

USDMXN rose another 1.0% to 18.368 on a day the dollar fell — +8.1% on the month, z=3.05, acceleration 2.1, the most extreme print in the book. Idiosyncratic peso stress that the Mexican equity bounce (EWW +1.8%) is not pricing.

The rate shock is still doing damage where it always does: 10-year real yield 2.91% (z=1.74, acceleration 1.23), 30-year mortgage 7.40% at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks, ITB -5.4% on the month and 12.6% below its 200-day, XHB/SPY at the 0th percentile.

The materials leg of the AI/power trade is being liquidated outright: REMX -4.6% on the day, -17.5% on the month at the 0th percentile and 32% below its 200-day; NLR -11.5% at the 0th; uranium -13.3%; solar -7.8%. Capex themes are losing their financing bid.

Breadth stays broken into bank earnings: RSP/SPY at the 11th percentile, IWM/SPY z=-1.50 at the 12th, DJT -4.2% on the month, KBE -6.3%, GS -13.1% with z=-1.89. A 99th-percentile index carried by fewer names each week.

trades.name: Software over silicon
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SMH: software over silicon
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long IGV / short SMH, 1:1 notional. Add CIBR as a 25% satellite on the long leg.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is splitting. Hardware is being liquidated through the Asian supply chain on positioning and dollar stress; recurring-revenue software and security are compounding and taking the index leadership. This expresses the de-rating of silicon without being short AI.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +8.8% in a week, +19.0% over three months, z=0.95, while SOXX fell 7.6% on the week and KOSPI -13.1%. IGV +9.6% on the month with relative strength +7.4%/+15.3%; CIBR +14.2% with acceleration z=2.05.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.178 (gives back the entire week's break), or SMH reclaiming its one-month high with Korea stabilising.

trades.name: US housing
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.40% mortgage, housing at 0th percentile
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy January 80-strike ITB puts; pair against long XLV if you need sector neutrality.
trades.thesis: Mortgage rates at 7.40% are a 100th-percentile financing shock that has not yet hit orders, cancellations or spec inventory. The equity has de-rated but the earnings have not. This is the cleanest transmission of the real-rate move.
trades.trigger: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +69bp on the month, z=2.06 with acceleration z=1.50, 100th percentile of 52 weeks; 10-year real yield 2.91% (+45bp month). ITB -5.4% on the month, 12.6% below its 200-day, 0th percentile; XHB/SPY 0th percentile; DHI 9.0% below its 200-day.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back under 7.00% or 10-year yield under 4.90%; or ITB closing back above its 200-day.

trades.name: Index convexity
trades.line: Long convexity: VIX3M 4th pctile vs MOVE +28% on the month
trades.expr: Buy 3-month SPX 5%-OTM puts (or a Dec 7400/6900 put spread); alternatively December VIX 20 calls. Size as 50-75bp of premium.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced for a calm index while the bond market is pricing a shock. With the index 7.6% above its 200-day, carried by a shrinking list, the convexity is mispriced against the breadth underneath it.
trades.trigger: VIX3M 17.93 at the 4th percentile of 52 weeks and VIX 15.32 at the 10th, against MOVE +28.3% on the month (z=1.50, acceleration 0.94) and SKEW 155 at the 81st percentile. Breadth: RSP/SPY 11th percentile, IWM/SPY z=-1.50.
trades.stop: Time/premium stop at 50% of premium paid; thesis invalidated if RSP/SPY and IWM/SPY turn up together with VIX3M above the 20th percentile.
trades.target: VIX above 22 / put spread at 3x premium.

trades.name: Brazil over Mexico
trades.line: Long EWZ vs short EWW: Brazil over Mexico
trades.expr: Long EWZ / short EWW, equal dollar. Cash-FX alternative: short USDBRL vs long USDMXN.
trades.thesis: EM is dispersing, not derisking. Brazil has currency, carry and the strongest equity momentum in the book; Mexico has the most extreme currency stress in the book and an equity market that hasn't discounted it.
trades.trigger: EWZ +14.0% on the month (z=1.60), BVSP +8.8% on the week, z=2.16, 100th percentile, with USDBRL -1.7% on the month. Against it, USDMXN +1.0% today to 18.368, +8.1% on the month, z=3.05, acceleration 2.1 — rising on a down-dollar day — while EWW is -2.8% on the month and rolling over.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.20, or the pair down 6% from entry.

trades.name: Energy equity vs the barrel
trades.line: Short XLE: energy equities at 100th pctile, barrel rolling
trades.expr: Short XLE or buy December 63-strike XLE puts; purer version is short XOP against a small long in crude futures.
trades.thesis: Energy equities are priced at the 52-week high while the commodity that pays for them has turned. Gasoline cracking is the tell that the product side, not just crude, is loosening — refining and E&P cash flows roll with a lag the equity hasn't taken.
trades.trigger: WTI -1.8% to 92.10 with acceleration z=-1.80 and -7.9% on the month; Brent -2.0%; gasoline -5.9% on the day, -6.3% on the month. Yet XLE sits at the 100th 52-week percentile, 16.5% above its 200-day, XOM at the 100th, while OIH is already -7.6% on the month and rolling over.

trades.name: Copper equity
trades.line: Long COPX: copper 97th pctile, dollar finally easing
trades.expr: Long COPX, or long FCX stock with January upside calls. Fund partly by trimming XME/gold-miner exposure.
trades.thesis: Copper is the one growth-sensitive asset that never flinched through the Korea unwind, and the miners have lagged the metal. A dollar that stops rising is the missing catalyst for the equity to catch the commodity.
trades.trigger: Copper +0.6% to 6.74, 97th percentile, +4.2% on the month; copper/gold at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks (z=1.30, acceleration 0.98). COPX turning_up but only 2.5% above its 200-day versus FCX +22.5% over three months. DXY -0.3%, first decline of the run.

trades.name: Bitcoin beta
trades.line: Long IBIT: bitcoin turning up off 83k
trades.expr: Long IBIT, 50-100bp notional; leveraged expression via January MSTR calls for those who want the convexity.
trades.thesis: The most liquidity-sensitive asset in the book bottomed before equities did and is turning up on the first sign the dollar squeeze is easing. Small size, asymmetric payoff from a depressed 52-week position.
trades.trigger: BTC +1.7% to 83,168, +8.2% on the month, +28.0% over three, state turning_up and relative strength to SPX +6.0%/+23.4%. ETH +2.2%, SOL +0.7%, MSTR +16.6% on the month — all turning_up — while BTC sits only at the 43rd 52-week percentile.
trades.stop: BTC back below 76,000 / IBIT below 43, which breaks the turning_up structure.
